This is a real production hosting business (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres). The free Minecraft product lets customers run a personal Minecraft server on a shared host (`freemc-host`, reached via SSH using DB-stored credentials — pattern below).

## The task

The customer asked for an in-dashboard command console for their free Minecraft server (things like `/gamemode creative`, and any other Minecraft/plugin command) — they say they asked for this before but don't see it anywhere in the dashboard/settings. Investigate what currently exists, then build it if it's genuinely missing.

## Where to look first

- `components/customer/freemc/` — the customer-facing dashboard (`FreeMcDashboard.tsx`, `FreeMinecraftTabContent.tsx`, `GameModeSelector.tsx`, `GameTypeGrid.tsx`, `SavedWorldsPanel.tsx`, `OverviewRedesigned.tsx`, and possibly an inventory-editor component)
- `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts`, `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts`, `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts` — server actions
- `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` — the core control library. It already has an internal `sendRcon` function that strips ANSI codes from responses and talks to the container via `docker exec <container> rcon-cli "<command>"` over SSH. Read this file to understand the existing RCON pattern before building anything new — don't reinvent it.
- `components/admin/FreeMinecraftControls.tsx` / `app/admin/free-minecraft/page.tsx` — the ADMIN side. It's possible a command console exists here but was never exposed to customers — check this specifically, since that would explain "I asked for this but don't see it" (it might exist somewhere the customer can't reach).

## If it doesn't exist, build it

Add a console/command input to the customer's free Minecraft dashboard (a new tab or section) that:
- Lets the customer type any command as they would in Minecraft chat (with or without a leading `/` — normalize it) and run it via RCON against THEIR OWN container only (never another customer's).
- Shows the command's response text back to them (the existing ANSI-stripped `sendRcon` return value).
- Rate-limits (there's already a `checkRateLimit` helper used elsewhere in this codebase — follow that convention).
- Validates the target server belongs to the requesting user (`requireUser()` + `db.freeMinecraftServer.findUnique({where:{userId: user.id}})` — follow the exact pattern used in `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts`).
- Sanitizes input before it reaches the shell — look at how `shellQuote` is used elsewhere in `free-minecraft-control.ts`/`lib/ssh-exec.ts` and use it identically. This command string ends up inside a `docker exec ... rcon-cli "..."` shell invocation, so injection here is a real security risk. Be careful and follow existing patterns exactly rather than improvising escaping.
- Style it consistent with the existing Nxeon dashboard (navy/violet/cyan theme, check other components in `components/customer/freemc/` for the exact classes/patterns already in use).

There's a real test container currently active: `mc-free-cmrztujaw0002hlazl58i3lsi` (owned by test user `cmrztujaw0002hlazl58i3lsi`) — safe for read-only checks (`list`, `help`, etc.) but avoid anything destructive since a real person is actively testing on it right now.

- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon-wt-console` to verify before finishing.
- Commit your changes (in that worktree, on branch `feature/freemc-console`) with a clear message. Do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging, do NOT run deploy/promote scripts — a human handles integration and production deployment separately, on purpose.

1	/**
2	 * Docker/RCON control primitives for free-tier Minecraft containers on
3	 * freemc-host — the free-tier equivalent of lib/game-control.ts, which speaks
4	 * to full Proxmox-VM game servers over SSH+tunnelled RCON. This is much
5	 * simpler: one SSH hop to the host, then `docker exec <container> ...` for
6	 * everything, using the CLI tools itzg/docker-minecraft-server already bundles
7	 * (rcon-cli, mc-monitor) instead of a hand-rolled RCON protocol client.
8	 *
9	 * Plain module (no "use server") — imported from both lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
10	 * and, in future, a worker sweep, same reasoning as lib/game-control.ts.
11	 */
12	import { scryptSync } from "node:crypto";
13	import type { Client } from "ssh2";
14	import { exec, execInput, shellQuote } from "./ssh-exec";
15	
16	/**
17	 * Deterministic per-server RCON password — HMAC-shaped via scrypt off
18	 * AUTH_SECRET, same derivation pattern as lib/crypto-box.ts's BYOK key (just a
19	 * different domain-separation salt). Never stored: computed identically at
20	 * container-creation time and every time we need to talk RCON to it, so a
21	 * restart/recreate never invalidates it and there's nothing to leak from the DB.
22	 */
23	export function rconPasswordFor(ownerId: string): string {
24	  const secret = process.env.AUTH_SECRET;
25	  if (!secret || !secret.trim()) throw new Error("AUTH_SECRET is not set — cannot derive RCON password");
26	  return scryptSync(secret, `nxeon-freemc-rcon:${ownerId}`, 24).toString("base64url");
27	}
28	
29	/** Run one command inside a container via `docker exec`. */
30	async function dockerExec(conn: Client, containerName: string, cmd: string, timeoutMs = 15_000) {
31	  return exec(conn, `docker exec ${shellQuote(containerName)} ${cmd}`, timeoutMs);
32	}
33	
34	export type ServerStatus = {
35	  running: boolean;
36	  players: { online: number; max: number } | null;
37	};
38	
39	/**
40	 * Best-effort status via mc-monitor (bundled in the image) — a plain status
41	 * ping, no RCON auth needed. A stopped/sleeping container (mc-router scaled it
42	 * to zero) just fails the docker exec, which reads as "not running", not an
43	 * error — that's the expected, common state for a free server nobody's on.
44	 */
45	export async function getFreeServerStatus(conn: Client, containerName: string): Promise<ServerStatus> {
46	  const inspect = await exec(
47	    conn,
48	    `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`,
49	    10_000,
50	  );
51	  if (inspect.code !== 0 || inspect.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
52	    return { running: false, players: null };
53	  }
54	  const status = await dockerExec(
55	    conn,
56	    containerName,
57	    "mc-monitor status --host localhost --port 25565 --json",
58	    10_000,
59	  );
60	  if (status.code !== 0) return { running: true, players: null }; // container up, MC still booting
61	  try {
62	    const parsed = JSON.parse(status.stdout);
63	    const p = parsed?.server_info?.players;
64	    if (typeof p?.online === "number" && typeof p?.max === "number") {
65	      return { running: true, players: { online: p.online, max: p.max } };
66	    }
67	  } catch {
68	    /* fall through */
69	  }
70	  return { running: true, players: null };
71	}
72	
73	export type RconResult = { ok: true; response: string } | { ok: false; error: string };
74	
75	// Some plugins (EssentialsX's /list override is the one that's bitten us)
76	// colorize their command output with raw ANSI escape codes, which the RCON
77	// protocol passes straight through as literal bytes in the response text —
78	// there's no terminal on the other end to interpret them. Confirmed live: a
79	// player name came back as "papiguapo\x1b[0m", which then failed every
80	// caller's name validation (it's not alphanumeric) and broke the inventory
81	// editor's "pick a valid player" check even with a real player selected.
82	// Stripped once here so every RCON consumer (players list, Console tab,
83	// Roles, inventory editor) gets clean text for free.
84	const ANSI_ESCAPE_RE = /\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/g;
85	
86	/** One RCON round-trip via the bundled rcon-cli — see lib/game-control.ts's
87	 *  validateRconCommand for the same input sanitation used on the paid path. */
88	export async function sendRcon(
89	  conn: Client,
90	  containerName: string,
91	  ownerId: string,
92	  command: string,
93	): Promise<RconResult> {
94	  const password = rconPasswordFor(ownerId);
95	  const r = await dockerExec(
96	    conn,
97	    containerName,
98	    `env RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(password)} rcon-cli ${shellQuote(command)}`,
99	    12_000,
100	  );
101	  if (r.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: r.stderr.trim() || "RCON command failed." };
102	  return { ok: true, response: r.stdout.replace(ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, "").trim() };
103	}

125	/** Reads /data/server.properties into a plain key->value map. */
126	export async function readServerProperties(
127	  conn: Client,
128	  containerName: string,
129	): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
130	  const r = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, "cat /data/server.properties", 10_000);
131	  if (r.code !== 0) return {};
132	  const out: Record<string, string> = {};
133	  for (const line of r.stdout.split("\n")) {
134	    if (!line || line.startsWith("#")) continue;
135	    const i = line.indexOf("=");
136	    if (i === -1) continue;
137	    out[line.slice(0, i).trim()] = line.slice(i + 1).trim();
138	  }
139	  return out;

142	/**
143	 * Writes a set of server.properties keys in place (sed-style line replace,
144	 * appending any key not already present) and restarts the container so the
145	 * itzg entrypoint's normal boot sequence picks the new values up — the image
146	 * only reads server.properties at startup (confirmed against the Minecraft
147	 * wiki: none of gamemode/motd/max-players/etc. persist a live RCON change back
148	 * to the file), so a restart is the only fully-reliable way to apply anything
149	 * here. Keys with a real live RCON equivalent (difficulty, whitelist on/off)
150	 * are ALSO pushed live by the caller for instant effect — see FIELD_LIVE_CMD.
151	 */
152	export async function writeServerProperties(
153	  conn: Client,
154	  containerName: string,
155	  changes: Record<string, string>,
156	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
157	  const current = await readServerProperties(conn, containerName);
158	  const merged = { ...current, ...changes };
159	  const body = Object.entries(merged)
160	    .map(([k, v]) => `${k}=${v}`)
161	    .join("\n");
162	  const write = await execInput(
163	    conn,
164	    `docker exec -i ${shellQuote(containerName)} sh -c 'cat > /data/server.properties'`,
165	    body + "\n",
166	    10_000,
167	  );
168	  if (write.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: write.stderr.trim() || "Could not write server.properties." };
169	  return { ok: true };
170	}

575	  containerName: string,
576	  ownerId: string,
577	  mode: FreeMcGameMode,
578	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
579	  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(mode.properties)) {

581	    if (liveCmd) await sendRcon(conn, containerName, ownerId, liveCmd).catch(() => {});
582	  }

584	  if (!write.ok) return { ok: false, error: write.error || "Could not write server.properties." };
585	  const restart = await exec(conn, `docker restart ${shellQuote(containerName)}`, 30_000);
586	  if (restart.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: restart.stderr || "docker restart failed" };

593	 * Polls until the Minecraft server inside `containerName` has actually
594	 * finished booting (its log prints "Done (Ns)!") or gives up.
595	 *
596	 * This exists because BOTH of the "is it ready" checks it replaces were too
597	 * shallow: `docker inspect ...State.Running` only proves the container
598	 * PROCESS hasn't crashed — a plugin-heavy boot spends 40-90s downloading and
599	 * loading before the game itself is reachable, and that whole window used to
600	 * read as "ready". Worse, mc-router's own wake check has the identical gap:
601	 * it just opens a raw TCP connection to :25565, and Minecraft's listener
602	 * binds early, well before world/plugin loading finishes — so the port looks
603	 * "up" long before the server can actually complete a client handshake. Both
604	 * gaps together are exactly what produced a real, reproduced-live customer
605	 * bug: switching to SkyBlock reported success, mc-router's TCP check passed
606	 * within seconds, and the customer's client still got "Failed to connect —
607	 * Timed out" because the server was still mid-boot. Polling the log line
608	 * itself is the only signal that means what it says.
609	 *
610	 * `docker restart` re-runs the exact same boot sequence as a fresh `docker
611	 * run`, so this same wait is needed after `applyModeProperties`'s restart
612	 * too, not just the initial container creation.
613	 */
614	async function waitForServerReady(
615	  conn: Client,
616	  containerName: string,
617	  timeoutMs = 110_000,
618	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
619	  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
620	  // First few seconds are the container just starting up (image entrypoint,
621	  // ownership fix, etc.) — no point polling logs before that's underway.
622	  await sleep(3_000);
623	  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
624	    const running = await exec(conn, `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' ${shellQuote(containerName)}`, 10_000);
625	    if (running.code !== 0 || running.stdout.trim() !== "true") {
626	      return { ok: false, error: "Container exited before finishing startup." };
627	    }
628	    const logs = await exec(conn, `docker logs ${shellQuote(containerName)} --tail 200 2>&1`, 10_000);
629	    if (/\bDone \([\d.]+s\)!/.test(logs.stdout)) return { ok: true };
630	    await sleep(3_000);
631	  }
632	  return { ok: false, error: "Server took too long to start." };
633	}

635	/**
636	 * Recreates a free server's container for a target GAME TYPE, with the given
637	 * GAME MODE applied on top (see mergeGameTypeAndMode) — the single shared
638	 * implementation every game-type-switching action (lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts,
639	 * lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts) builds its `docker run` from, so the LEVEL /
640	 * mode-controlled-key handling below can't drift between call sites the way
641	 * three independently hand-rolled `docker run` commands eventually would.
642	 *
643	 * Sets `-e LEVEL=<gameTypeKey>` so this type's world lives in its own
644	 * `<LEVEL>`/`<LEVEL>_nether`/`<LEVEL>_the_end` folder set inside the SAME
645	 * /data volume mount, never touching another type's saved world (confirmed
646	 * live — see the module-doc note above FREEMC_GAME_TYPES). Deliberately does
647	 * NOT env-bake gamemode/hardcore/difficulty (see envForGameType) — those are
648	 * applied in a second pass via applyModeProperties, once the container is
649	 * confirmed alive, so a later mode-only restart can always change them
650	 * cleanly without a recreate.
651	 *
652	 * Verifies liveness twice — once ~15s after `docker run` (long enough for an
653	 * init-time plugin/version failure to have already killed it), once more
654	 * ~8s after the follow-up mode-properties restart — and never throws; the
655	 * caller decides what a failure means (typically: roll back to the
656	 * account's previous type/mode).
657	 */
658	export async function recreateGameTypeContainer(
659	  conn: Client,
660	  params: {
661	    containerName: string;
662	    dataPath: string;
663	    subdomain: string;
664	    domain: string;
665	    ramMb: number;
666	    ownerId: string;
667	    gameType: FreeMcGameType;
668	    gameTypeKey: string;
669	    gameMode: FreeMcGameMode;
670	    /** Extra env vars layered on top of the type's own (e.g. the Mod Menu's
671	     *  merged MODRINTH_PROJECTS list) — last-write-wins over the type's env. */
672	    extraEnv?: Record<string, string>;
673	  },
674	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
675	  const jvmRatio = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? 0.7 : 0.85; // plugins need more non-heap headroom — see FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION's neighboring history
676	  const cpus = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? 2 : 1; // see recreatePresetContainer's note on mc-router's fixed 60s wake timeout
677	  // The global free_minecraft_ram_mb setting (1024 by default) is sized for
678	  // the properties-only presets — plugins-kind ones (EssentialsX + LuckPerms
679	  // + Vault + a type's own plugins, up to 6 loaded dimensions on something
680	  // like SkyBlock) run noticeably heavier and were found live to OOM-kill a
681	  // short while AFTER printing "Done" at that ceiling — not during boot, so
682	  // the old shallow "still alive 15s after docker run" check never caught it,
683	  // and the fix wasn't the plugins themselves (confirmed by re-testing with
684	  // WorldEdit removed — same crash, same timing) or --cpus. It really is a
685	  // sizing problem: 1536m/0.7 ran the same SkyBlock config stable for 100s+
686	  // post-boot with ONE player — but confirmed live it's still not enough
687	  // once a SECOND player joins: memory climbed to 90% (1.355GB/1.5GB) during
688	  // the second player's own island-creation schematic paste (world-gen +
689	  // chunk load + plugin bookkeeping for two islands across up to 6
690	  // dimensions at once), and the container was killed twice in that window
691	  // before settling. 2560m/0.7 gives real headroom for that case; the free
692	  // tier is a shared/social product, so "two friends on one server" is the
693	  // common case, not an edge case. Bump container memory for plugin-kind
694	  // presets specifically rather than raising the global default (which
695	  // properties-only presets don't need).
696	  const ramMb = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? Math.max(params.ramMb, 2560) : params.ramMb;
697	  const jvmMb = Math.max(256, Math.round(ramMb * jvmRatio));
698	
699	  const envVars = { ...envForGameType(params.gameType), ...(params.extraEnv ?? {}), LEVEL: params.gameTypeKey };
700	  const envFlags = Object.entries(envVars)
701	    .map(([k, v]) => `-e ${k}=${shellQuote(v)}`)
702	    .join(" ");
703	
704	  await exec(conn, `docker rm -f ${shellQuote(params.containerName)}`, 30_000);
705	  const cmd = [
706	    "docker run -d",
707	    `--name ${shellQuote(params.containerName)}`,
708	    "--network freemc",
709	    `--memory=${ramMb}m --memory-swap=${ramMb}m --cpus=${cpus}`,
710	    `--label mc-router.host=${shellQuote(`${params.subdomain}.${params.domain}`)}`,
711	    `-v ${shellQuote(params.dataPath)}:/data`,
712	    `-e EULA=TRUE -e TYPE=${params.gameType.type ?? "VANILLA"} -e ONLINE_MODE=FALSE`,
713	    params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? `-e VERSION=${shellQuote(FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION)}` : "",
714	    `-e MEMORY=${jvmMb}m`,
715	    `-e ENABLE_RCON=true -e RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(rconPasswordFor(params.ownerId))}`,
716	    envFlags,
717	    "itzg/minecraft-server",
718	  ].join(" ");
719	  const run = await exec(conn, cmd, 90_000); // plugin downloads can take longer than a plain boot
720	  if (run.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: run.stderr || "docker run failed" };
721	
722	  const ready = await waitForServerReady(conn, params.containerName);
723	  if (!ready.ok) return ready;
724	
725	  // IridiumSkyblock ships with `islandCreateOnJoin: false` — a customer who
726	  // joins fresh just spawns in the plain overworld terrain (which, since
727	  // that's Paper's stock generator, looks exactly like Vanilla), with no
728	  // floating island and no indication one exists to create. Confirmed live:
729	  // a customer reported "joined the server but it has vanilla loaded even
730	  // though I chose skyblock" — this is why. The config file only exists
731	  // after the plugin's first boot (it writes its own defaults), so this has
732	  // to run as a post-boot patch, not something bakeable into the image/env.
733	  // Patched HERE — right after the first readiness wait, BEFORE
734	  // applyModeProperties's own restart below — so that ONE restart picks up
735	  // both this and the mode properties together. An earlier version patched
736	  // this AFTER applyModeProperties with its own separate restart+wait, which
737	  // meant a SkyBlock switch chained three full boot-and-wait cycles back to
738	  // back (each 40-90s) — confirmed live to run past whatever the browser/
739	  // client was willing to wait for, so the switch would actually succeed
740	  // server-side a couple minutes later while the customer had already seen
741	  // a timeout/error and given up. Two cycles instead of three meaningfully
742	  // shortens that window; a config patch with no plugin process running yet
743	  // to pick it up costs nothing extra by itself.
744	  //
745	  // `islandCreateOnJoin` alone was not the whole bug: it only makes the
746	  // plugin create the island in the background. Whether the player actually
747	  // gets TELEPORTED there is a separate key, `spawnOnIsland`, which also
748	  // ships `false` — so even with an island silently created, the player was
749	  // left standing in that same plain default-generator "skyblock" level,
750	  // which is exactly the "shows active on skyblock but loads vanilla world"
751	  // report. Both keys have to be true for a fresh join to actually land the
752	  // player on their island.
753	  //
754	  // `paster: "worldedit"` is a third default-config landmine: this server
755	  // stack never installs WorldEdit (the boot log warns "selected paster
756	  // [worldedit] is not available, available choices are [internalAsync]"),
757	  // and running `/is create` against that misconfiguration killed the whole
758	  // Minecraft process outright — instant death, no Java exception, no JVM
759	  // crash dump, exit code -1 from mc-server-runner. Confirmed live: with
760	  // `paster: "internalAsync"` (the only paster actually available) patched
761	  // in, `/is create` completes normally. internalAsync is the plugin's own
762	  // built-in pasting implementation and needs no other plugin installed.
763	  if (params.gameTypeKey === "skyblock") {
764	    const patch = await exec(
765	      conn,
766	      `docker exec ${shellQuote(params.containerName)} sed -i ` +
767	        `-e 's/islandCreateOnJoin: false/islandCreateOnJoin: true/' ` +
768	        `-e 's/spawnOnIsland: false/spawnOnIsland: true/' ` +
769	        `-e 's/paster: "worldedit"/paster: "internalAsync"/' ` +
770	        `/data/plugins/IridiumSkyblock/configuration.yml`,
771	      10_000,
772	    );
773	    if (patch.code !== 0) {
774	      console.error("[free-minecraft] SkyBlock island-spawn config patch failed (non-fatal):", patch.stderr);
775	    }
776	  }
777	
778	  const modeApplied = await applyModeProperties(conn, params.containerName, params.ownerId, params.gameMode);
779	  if (!modeApplied.ok) return { ok: false, error: modeApplied.error || "Could not apply the active game mode." };
780	
781	  // applyModeProperties ends in a `docker restart`, which re-runs the exact
782	  // same boot sequence as the `docker run` above — needs the same real
783	  // readiness wait, not a fixed few-second sleep. This restart is also what
784	  // picks up the SkyBlock config patch above, if it ran.
785	  const readyAfterMode = await waitForServerReady(conn, params.containerName);
786	  if (!readyAfterMode.ok) {
787	    return { ok: false, error: readyAfterMode.error || "Server didn't come back up after applying the active game mode." };
788	  }
789	
790	  return { ok: true };
